findings.claim: Defining NETFRAMEWORK strips ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from every generated formatter and resolver, although the attribute exists on supported modern .NET Framework targets. Consequently, code generated for .NET Framework remains included in coverage, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated; conditional omission is only needed where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedTypesStillGetCoverageExclusion. It runs the generator with NETFRAMEWORK defined and asserts that the compiled generated resolver has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; the current guard makes the assertion fail.

findings.claim: A consumer that already applied [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to its partial generated resolver now gets a second copy from ResolverTemplate. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiple attributes, and attributes from partial declarations are combined, so previously valid source fails with CS0579 instead of compiling.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.UserAttributedResolverDoesNotProduceDuplicateAttribute. It compiles a partial [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] that already has [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], with the generated attribute active, and asserts that no CS0579 diagnostic is produced.
